transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… what finally made me call was that some mornings I wake up and think, well, maybe it would’ve been easier if I just hadn’t woken up at all. I don’t have some plan to hurt myself or anything like that, but the thought scared me.

I almost didn’t come in—I kept telling myself everyone has bad days, and then I got distracted cleaning out an old drawer of papers from when I was working, and that took half the afternoon—but it’s been sitting with me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, most days for the past two weeks or more?

Yes… I think so. I still make myself go to things, like my book club, and there’s a dance night I’ve always liked—well, I used to like it more, anyway. I’ll get dressed and go, because otherwise I’d just be sitting at home, and then someone will be talking about some novel and I realize I’m just sort of… there, but not there. Like I’m watching from behind glass.

Even the garden, which usually perks me up, or cooking something for the neighbors—little things that used to give me a lift—they just don’t seem to do much lately. I keep doing them, but it feels flatter.
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these feelings of sadness or loss of interest been present most days for at least two years?

No, not two years. It’s more like… about a month, I’d say. It started after my sister died unexpectedly. I keep thinking of things I should’ve asked her, you know—little things, like where she got this old recipe box we used to joke about, and then I realize I can’t ask her. But yes, about a month.
